title: The Agitators in Galatia
lead: The 'Judaizers' is the traditional name for the people who pressed Paul's Gentile converts in Galatia to be circumcised and to keep Jewish law. Paul never names them; he calls them 'some people who are upsetting you' (Galatians 1:7) and 'false brothers' (Galatians 2:4). Who they were, where they came from and what they taught is reconstructed from Paul's replies, a method called mirror-reading.

sections.b: Common views: Jewish Christians from Jerusalem or Judea who held that Gentile believers must become proselytes (the Pharisee believers of Acts 15:5); Jewish-Christian missionaries from Antioch's circle; local Gentile Christians who had begun to judaize; or, in Mark Nanos's reading, Jewish non-Christian synagogue leaders who pressed Gentile Christians to complete conversion so as to be accepted as legitimate in the Jewish community. The word 'Judaizer' comes from Galatians 2:14, where Paul says Cephas compels the Gentiles to 'judaize', that is, live in the Jewish way.
